open.subject: A probe string that QUOTES CODE reads as a code site to every sweep that scans source, and each one has to be disposed by hand
open.the_shape: rx() registrations state the strings a regex must match and must not match, and for a regex that reads source those strings ARE source: `matches: ['s.matchAll(re)', 'new RegExp(x)', 's.match(re)']` in blanket-audit.mjs was read by guard-sweep's [extract] selector as an extraction site with no disposition. One phantom on this cycle, disposed as [G-149]. Every future probe that quotes code lands the same way, in whichever sweep's selector its text happens to satisfy.
open.why_it_is_not_settled_here: The two obvious remedies are both worse than the symptom. Teaching every source-scanning sweep to skip lines inside an rx() spec is a change to four selectors at once, and a selector taught to ignore a region is a selector that can be made to ignore a real site by moving it there. Assembling probe strings from fragments so they do not look like code makes the probe unreadable, and an unreadable probe is one nobody checks against the regex it is meant to prove. Neither is worth doing on one instance.
open.the_measurement_that_would_settle_it: How many phantoms adoption produces per registered regex. Twenty-four registrations produced one. If that ratio holds, hand disposition is cheaper than any mechanism; if a later cycle adopts widely and the count rises, the shape of the fix is a shared "this is data, not code" marker that every source scanner in the engine reads from one place, rather than four independent skip rules.

open.raised_in: Prompt 52 commit 2, deriving 433-D's subject from its printed page
open.subject: THE SUBJECT AXIS ANSWERS PER FORM AND 433-D'S SUBJECT IS PER RECORD. Every reuse verdict this engine has made rests on a form fixing its subject in print. 433-D does not.
open.the_shape: 433-D prints NO eligibility text — six phrases searched across all four drawn pages, all six return zero. What it prints instead points BOTH ways at once: "Social Security or Employer Identification Number (SSN/ITIN/EIN)" on one line, "(Taxpayer)" and "(Spouse)" beneath it; a signature row carrying both "Title (if Corporate Officer or Partner)" and "Spouse's signature (if a joint liability)"; an assistance line naming "Individual - Self-Employed/Business Owners, Businesses" and "Individuals - Wage Earners"; and an IRS-use block offering an IMF review and a BMF review. So one filed 433-D is about a natural person and the next is about a corporation, and nothing printed on the form distinguishes them — only which identifier the filer wrote.
open.what_it_does_to_the_register: 433-D COINCIDES WITH ALL FIVE registered forms, including with 433-A and 433-B, which are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with each other. That is not an inconsistency in adapters/pdf/maps/_subjects.cross-form.json; it is the true relation, and the register now records it with the asymmetry named on each of the five pairs rather than levelled into the five coincidences already there. 433-A and 433-F coincide because BOTH are about the individual and neither admits anything else; 433-D coincides with them because it ADMITS the individual among others. Two different relations wearing one word is the thing that register exists to keep apart.
open.why_it_is_a_problem_today: [R-06]: the naming test runs on the SUBJECT and not on the question. On the other five forms that test is answerable once for the whole form, which is exactly how 433-B(OIC)'s 113 form-specific names and 433-B's nine reuses were settled. On 433-D it is not answerable once. A 433-D cell that looks like an existing individual property and a 433-D cell that looks like an existing entity property may BOTH be right, for different filers, through the same printed cell — and a property cannot hold two values for one filer at one moment, which is the whole of the test.
open.the_ruling: RAISED AND NOT RESOLVED. It is a question about what may be built and it must be answered BEFORE 433-D's crosswalk, not during it — the same ordering the subject register's own `_how_to_use_it` states. Resolving it inside an INTAKE, in a cycle whose scope line excludes the crosswalk, is the adjacent change [R-12] says to expect to reproduce the defect class.
open.what_is_actually_being_asked: THREE CANDIDATE SHAPES, none chosen here, each with what it would cost. (1) TREAT 433-D AS INDIVIDUAL-ONLY and refuse EIN records — cheap, and it silently drops the business installment agreement, which is a real filing. (2) SPLIT EVERY AMBIGUOUS KEY into an individual-subject property and an entity-subject property — safe on the subject axis and expensive against a headroom of 116. (3) MAKE THE SUBJECT A RECORD-LEVEL DISCRIMINATOR, one declared input that routes each ambiguous key to the individual property or the entity property — closest to how `record_shape` already routes 433-A(OIC), and the only one that costs nothing extra per fact. open.subject: assert-fixture-authorship's whole-directory hold is correct against the generator and defenceless against a second copy of itself
open.the_shape: adapters/pdf/assert-fixture-authorship.mjs re-runs each fixture's declared generator to ask whether the generator is still its sole author. Generators WRITE INTO samples/, so the check reads every sample into memory first and restores all of them in a `finally`. Its header records why the hold is in memory rather than on disk, and that reasoning is sound: bytes in a Buffer cannot be removed by anything the generator does.
open.why_it_is_a_problem_today: THE HOLD IS PER PROCESS AND THE DIRECTORY IS SHARED. Two concurrent invocations each snapshot samples/, each run generators into it, and each restore its own snapshot. If process B regenerates a fixture between A's snapshot and A's restore, A's restore writes B's regenerated bytes back as though they were the committed ones — permanently, in the working tree, with both processes reporting success. Nothing in either run can see it: each restore verifies against ITS OWN snapshot and both verifications pass. Only `git status` shows it. The tool is reached by validate-map.mjs, which is gate step 3, so this fires whenever two gates, two coverage runs, or a gate and a sweep overlap — which is the obvious thing to do to a suite whose full pass is upwards of twenty minutes.
open.observed: OBSERVED, NOT REASONED. Three `node adapters/pdf/declaration-coverage.mjs <form>` runs were started in the background while `npm run sweeps` ran in the foreground. samples/433boi.slice3.sample.json was left holding scratchpad/author-record-shape-fixtures.mjs's output while claiming scratchpad/author-slice3-fixture.mjs as its generator — account balances rounded to whole dollars, business_income_expense_route removed. validate-map.mjs then exited 2 on 433boi, 433d and 433f with five CO-AUTHORSHIP UNDECLARED problems, and `npm run sweeps:deep` exited 2 reporting assert-fixture-authorship NOT REPORTED on all six forms. `git checkout -- samples/433boi.slice3.sample.json` restored it and every one of those runs went green.
open.why_it_is_not_fixed_here: A LOCK IS A CHANGE TO THE INSTRUMENT THAT STANDS OVER EVERY FIXTURE IN THE TREE, mid-provisioning, and [R-12] is the rule that a refactor of a guard is a change to the guard. The [D-11] precedent is explicit about this shape: rewriting a guard as an adjacent change during a provisioning pass has twice reproduced the class it was meant to close. Recorded with its observation so it cannot evaporate ([R-20]).
open.the_shape_of_a_fix: A whole-directory advisory lock taken before the snapshot and released after the restore-and-verify, so a second invocation waits rather than interleaving; and the restore verification extended to compare against the file's git-committed bytes where the file is tracked, so a hold that captured someone else's output fails loudly rather than blessing it. Both are checkable and both would have fired on the run above.
open.what_this_item_is_NOT: It is NOT a claim that the tree was ever corrupted by a committed run. Every recorded pass of this engine has been serial, and the working-tree damage above was caused by this cycle's own pre-flight running things in parallel to save wall clock. What the item records is that nothing in the engine would have said so — the corruption was found by `git status`, and `git status` is not a check this engine runs.
open.status: OPEN - observed and reported, not fixed.

resolved.subject: exclusion-sweep.mjs builds its predicate universe from NAMES, so a local const in any swept file makes every same-named call anywhere in the engine an exclusion site - including calls to built-in methods
resolved.the_mechanism: enginePredicates() collects every `const|let|function NAME = (` across the swept files into one flat set of STRINGS. exclusionSites() then scans every exclusion position - `if (X) continue`, `.filter(f => ...)` and three more shapes - and attributes the site to any called name that is in that set. Neither step asks WHERE the name was defined, whether the call is in the same file, or whether the callee is a bare identifier or a method on an object.
what_it_did_twice: FIRST, SILENTLY, FOR THREE SLICES. Register entry [X-16] disposed of `if (!field.isChecked()) continue;` in adapters/pdf/verify-appearances.mjs. isChecked is PDFCheckBox.prototype.isChecked, a pdf-lib method, and pdf-lib is not swept. It was in the universe only because adapters/pdf/run-form-gate.mjs happened to declare an unrelated local `const isChecked = (target) =>` inside gate step 11. Hoisting that local for [B9] turned it into an object property, the name left the universe, and the orphan check finally named the entry. The entry was RETIRED in commit 1 of this prompt with its text kept verbatim.

THEN IMMEDIATELY, LOUDLY, IN THE OTHER DIRECTION. adapters/pdf/assert-completeness-counters.mjs was added in commit 3 with a local `const get = (id) =>`. On the next run the sweep reported UNREGISTERED for `catOf.get(b.entry) !== 'new'` at adapters/hubspot/reclassify-against-backbone.mjs:200 - a call to Map.prototype.get, in a file with no connection to the new one. One new local in one file made a built-in method call in another file an unregistered exclusion and took the gate down.
resolved.why_the_second_direction_is_the_useful_o: The first direction hides a real site behind a false disposition and nothing complains. The second is a STOP and complains immediately. So the failure mode that matters is the FIRST: any register entry in PREDICATES may be disposing of a call that is only in scope by accident, and the way to find out is not to wait for the accident to end.
resolved.the_fix_is_not_here: Distinguishing a bare call from a method call means reading `X.name(` differently from `name(`, which is a change to exclusionSites() - the function every entry in PREDICATES is measured by - and its no-op path would have to be proved across all 25 registered entries and every site they cover in the same run. That is a change to a guard and not slice work.

resolved.what_it_got_right: The mechanism, exactly as written. enginePredicates() did collect every definition across the swept files into one flat set of STRINGS, exclusionSites() did attribute a site to any called name in that set, and neither step asked where the name was defined or whether the calling file could reach it. REACHABILITY kills both accidents on its own and never has to look at the call syntax: isChecked is neither defined in nor imported into verify-appearances.mjs, and `get` is neither defined in nor imported into reclassify-against-backbone.mjs, so both sites leave the universe without any judgement about what a dot means. An exclusion site carries `definedIn`. Every PREDICATES entry names its defining module (one, or a list where the same one-line predicate is genuinely declared in several files), and sitesFor() matches on the pair. The orphan check, the completeness check and [EX-90] all moved to the pair.

resolved.raised_in: Prompt 41, commit 1 — split off [D-08] when reachability closed the half that mattered
resolved.subject: exclusion-sweep.mjs still does not distinguish a bare call from a method call, so `x.norm(...)` matches a `norm` defined in the SAME file
resolved.the_mechanism: CALL is /\b([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*\(/g over the text of an exclusion position, which matches the identifier before a "(" whether or not a "." precedes it. Reachability now requires the name to be defined in or imported into the calling file, so the cross-file accident is gone. What survives is the same-file case: a file that defines `const norm = ...` and elsewhere calls `someMap.norm(...)` in an exclusion position attributes that site to its own predicate.
resolved.why_it_is_smaller_than_D_08: The dangerous direction of [D-08] was a register entry standing over a call the file could not even see — a disposition sound only while a name collision held, in a file nobody would think to check. This one is confined to a single file, where the definition and the call are both in front of whoever reads the disposition, and the entry names the file. It can still be wrong; it can no longer be wrong invisibly.
resolved.what_would_close_it: Read the character before the identifier and refuse a site where it is a ".". That is a change to exclusionSites(), which every entry in PREDICATES is measured by, so its no-op path has to be proved across all twenty-eight entries and every site they cover in the same run — the same standard the reachability change was held to, and the reason it is not being done in the same commit as slice work.
resolved.the_current_exposure: Zero sites in this tree are known to be in this state. That is an observation and not a proof: nothing enumerates it, which is itself part of what would close this.
resolved.what_was_actually_asked_for_and_what_was: The ruling asked for [D-09]'s exposure to be ENUMERATED or declared underivable with a reason. It is enumerated. adapters/pdf/enumerate-shadowing.mjs classifies every attribution `exclusionSites()` makes — imported, so it counts that instrument's own output and not a copy — by whether the attributed predicate appears in the site's captured text as a plain call (BARE, sound), only ever as a method call (METHOD, a [D-09] instance) or not at all (ABSENT, an UNREADABLE STOP rather than a zero). 51 attributions across 14 files: 51 sound, 0 instances, 0 unreadable. The sentence "zero known instances - stated as an observation, not a proof" is replaced by a number derived on every validate-map run and every `npm run sweeps`.
resolved.the_canary_because_the_expected_answer_i: An enumerator whose answer is zero is the easiest object in a repo to get wrong, because a broken one and a clean tree print the same number. Seven synthetic classifier behaviours fire on every run and the count is not printed at all if any fails — including that a longer name is not matched by a shorter one, that an optional-chained method reads METHOD, and that null text reads ABSENT rather than 0. Proved beyond the synthetic strings too: a real `bag.norm(xs)` planted in a swept file was found and named with its file, line and defining module, and the enumeration returned to 0 when the plant was removed.
resolved.what_this_does_NOT_do_and_what_is_still_: IT DOES NOT CLOSE THE MECHANISM. exclusionSites() still does not read the character before the identifier, so a `x.norm(...)` written into an exclusion position tomorrow would be attributed tomorrow. What has changed is that it would be REPORTED tomorrow instead of discovered later. Closing the mechanism is a change to the function every one of the twenty-eight register entries is measured by, and its no-op path has to be proved across all of them in the same run — carried on as [D-10] so the remaining work is not read as done.

resolved.the_shape: hs-fetch-433boi.mjs, run against a live contact, correctly reached its own "REFUSING TO WRITE - 1 problem(s)" and called process.exit(3). What the caller saw was 3221226505 through spawnSync and 127 through a shell, preceded by "Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING), file src\win\async.c, line 76". The declared code never leaves the process. It is NOT a defect in that fetcher: it reproduces in five lines with no fetcher present — import hs, await one request, call process.exit(3) — so the fetcher is only the first tool this cycle happened to drive down a post-portal STOP path.
resolved.the_measured_population: SEVENTY-TWO process.exit() sites across TWENTY-TWO files in adapters/hubspot/, counted by grep over every file importing hs-lib.mjs on 2026-08-25. Not all are post-portal — a usage exit before the first request is safe, and the reproduction needed a completed request — but that split has NOT been measured, and the figure quoted here is the one that has been: 72 is the population an audit would have to walk, not the count of broken sites. Quoting a smaller unmeasured number would be the figure without its universe that [R-07] names.
resolved.why_it_is_a_problem_today: THE SCARY HALF IS NOT THE FETCHERS. hs-provision.mjs, hs-purge-properties.mjs, hs-purge-contacts.mjs and hs-teardown-contact.mjs are permanent or destructive, and each carries post-portal STOP paths whose declared code is what a caller would branch on. A caller testing `status === 2` sees 127 and takes the wrong branch; a caller testing `status !== 0` still catches it, which is why nothing has surfaced. An abort is also not a clean stop — whatever the tool had not flushed is gone — and "it exited non-zero" is a weaker fact than the one the tool was written to state.
resolved.what_was_proved: THE FIX IS KNOWN AND IT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN GUESSED, WHICH IS WHY THIS ITEM IS SAFE TO CARRY. Candidate A — `process.exitCode = 3` with no process.exit() call — exits with the real code 3 after a natural drain of 382 ms. Candidate B — close the global undici dispatcher and then call process.exit(3) — STILL ABORTS, so the obvious repair is the wrong one and an unmeasured fix would have shipped it. A third shape also works and preserves the halting semantics the call sites rely on: set process.exitCode, throw a sentinel, and swallow only that sentinel in an unhandledRejection handler.
resolved.the_ruling: REPORTED IN FULL AND NOT RESOLVED, under [R-20], and the reason is [R-12]. The identity block is the clear case: "Social Security or Employer Identification Number (SSN/ITIN/EIN)" is one caption over one cell, and an SSN goes in it for a natural person and an EIN for an entity. TWO — SUBJECT-INDEPENDENT. A bank routing number is a bank routing number on either, and 69 of the 83 stems derive this way. THREE — SUBJECT-CONDITIONAL, WHICH IS THE ONE WITH NO SLOT. The cell EXISTS for one subject and not the other, and its printed caption says so in as many words: "Title (if Corporate Officer or Partner)" is drawn only to be filled when an entity is the filer, and "Spouse's signature (if a joint liability)" only when a natural person is. Neither caption admits both subjects — each admits exactly ONE — so the ruling's test classifies both as subject-INDEPENDENT, which is the opposite of the truth about them. resolved.why_it_matters_before_the_construct_and_: BECAUSE THE TWO KINDS EARN DIFFERENT CHECKS, AND THE CHECK IS THE CONSTRUCT. A subject-CONDITIONAL cell needs no second property at all; it needs an EMPTINESS assertion, which is the shape adapters/pdf/record-shape.mjs already carries as `operands_empty_and_total_present`. Building the discriminator as a binary would either split the conditional cells into two properties each — spending headroom on a property that can only ever be empty — or leave them unchecked, so that an entity record carrying a spouse signature would pass. Every other form in this repo pins its revision against text drawn on the page, and confirm-form-revision-from-page-bytes is a standing rule. A pin read from an XFA packet is not evidence of the same kind, and treating the two as interchangeable would quietly weaken the rule for every form.
resolved.the_ruling: Do not attempt it, and do not fold it into any prompt for the other forms. It becomes a SEPARATE FEASIBILITY TRACK after 433-A(OIC), 433-B(OIC), 433-B and 433-D, and the first question that track must answer is whether we fill an XFA form at all or author a static replica.

resolved.what_this_item_got_RIGHT: BOTH HALVES, AND THE SHARPER HALF WAS SHARPER THAN IT KNEW. (a) "Nothing this engine does has an input" is exactly true and the reason is now measured: pdf-lib deletes /XFA from the AcroForm on getForm(), and on 433-H that leaves ZERO fields where on 433-D it leaves 168. (b) "A pin read from an XFA packet is not evidence of the same kind" was right, and the drawn page is worse than the item supposed — it carries no revision, no catalogue number and no form number at all, only 332 characters of Adobe Reader placeholder. (c) The ruling that this becomes a SEPARATE FEASIBILITY TRACK whose first question is "do we fill an XFA form at all or author a static replica" set exactly the right question, and it is the question answered below.
resolved.what_this_item_got_WRONG: ONE THING, AND IT WIDENS THE OPTIONS RATHER THAN NARROWING THEM. "This form cannot be mapped by the current engine at all" is true of the FILL engine and false of the tree as a whole. pdfjs-dist, ALREADY A DEPENDENCY IN THIS REPO AT ^6.2.108, renders this form: with enableXfa it reports isPureXfa true, lays the template out to EIGHT pages rather than the one static page pdf-lib and a default pdfjs both see, and returns a complete XFA HTML tree. The item was written from a reading taken with XFA disabled, and the one-page answer that reading gives is what made the form look inert. It is not inert; it is unreachable by the AcroForm path only.
resolved.what_433H_asks: 331 fields in the template packet, by ui kind {"numericEdit":172,"textEdit":130,"checkButton":26,"signature":2,"dateTimeEdit":1}. Structurally it is 433-F PLUS AN INSTALMENT AGREEMENT REQUEST: sections A (Accounts/Lines of Credit), B (Real Estate), C (Other Assets), D (Credit Cards), Investments, Digital Assets, E (Employment Information), income, and G (Monthly Necessary Living Expenses) reproduce 433-F's section lettering and its group set — 433-F's map already declares bank_accounts, investments, real_estate, other_assets, credit_cards and digital_assets — while Part 1 lines 1 to 9 are the instalment agreement request, whose routing and account cells are 433-D's comb decomposition exactly: NINE routing digits and SEVENTEEN account digits on both forms.
resolved.what_it_asks_that_the_six_mapped_forms_D: THE "I R S ALLOWED" COLUMN. 433-H prints every monthly living expense TWICE — "Actual Monthly Expenses" beside "I R S Allowed" — 32 cells in each column. No mapped form draws that pair: 433-F's expense table is single-column and carries no key matching /allow/, and 433-A(OIC)'s three allowance keys are specific deductions rather than a per-row allowed column. IT IS NOT A TAXPAYER FACT. The allowed figure is the IRS Collection Financial Standard, which this repo already holds at adapters/pdf/maps/irs-standards-2026.json, so the column is DERIVABLE from data in the tree rather than a fact the backbone lacks. Beyond it the field-level comparison surfaces CANDIDATES and not findings, for the reason adapters/hubspot/reclassify-against-backbone.mjs states in its own header — deciding that two differently-named facts are one fact cannot be done mechanically — and the comparison was run against all six maps and all 584 live irs433* properties rather than against one predecessor.
resolved.the_route_that_pdf_lib_forecloses: MEASURED ON THIS PACKET RATHER THAN INFERRED FROM THE PROJECT'S GENERAL KNOWLEDGE THAT pdf-lib STRIPS XFA. getForm() deletes /XFA from the AcroForm dict of every form in this tree, 433-H included. On the six mapped forms that is HARMLESS AND IS WHY THE ENGINE WORKS — each is a HYBRID XFA form carrying an /XFA array of 18 beside a populated AcroForm, so removing the XFA leaves 168 to 515 fillable widgets untouched. On 433-H it leaves ZERO, and the 3,218,407-byte input saves to 3,208,930 bytes of one placeholder page with an empty AcroForm and no XFA at all — STRICTLY WORSE THAN THE INPUT, because the only thing that could have rendered it is gone. THE ENGINE HAS NEVER FILLED AN XFA FORM. It has always filled the AcroForm shadow the IRS's static-XFA forms ship with, and 433-H ships without one.
resolved.route_A_fill_the_datasets: RULED OUT AS A FILL ROUTE, ON A CEILING DERIVED FROM THE TEMPLATE'S OWN DIRECTIVES. The blank ships with SEVEN packets (preamble, config, template, localeSet, xmpmeta, xfdf, postamble) against nine on every mapped form: no datasets packet and no form packet, so it ships unmerged and a processor must lay it out at open time. A datasets packet CAN be injected — the /XFA array is editable at the object level provided getForm() is never called — and pdfjs BINDS IT: a sentinel written into a flat <form1> data hierarchy came back in the rendered XFA tree. BUT 186 OF THE 331 FIELDS CARRY <bind match="none"/>, which is the template declining to connect the field to the data DOM, and no conforming processor overrides it. The negative control proved it on this form: the same injection that reached a no-bind field did not reach a match="none" one. The ceiling is 145 of 331. A route that can populate at most that share of a form is not a fill route.
resolved.route_A_prime_write_the_template: WORKS, AND IS RULED OUT ON WHAT IT MAKES RATHER THAN ON WHETHER IT WORKS. Writing <value><text>…</text></value> into a field definition inside the TEMPLATE packet renders that value — proved on the very field that refuses data binding. It has no ceiling: it reaches all 331. What it produces is the IRS's form DEFINITION with our values written into it, which is a different object from a filled form, and it collides head-on with the revision problem below: a revision read back out of a packet WE EDITED is not a pin, it is a copy of what we wrote. Recorded as available and not adopted.
resolved.route_the_prompt_did_not_name_RENDER_RAT: INJECT, RENDER, PRINT. pdfjs-dist ^6.2.108 is already a dependency here and already renders this form to eight laid-out pages. Data goes in by route A for the 145 bindable fields or by route A-prime for all 331; the render is then printed to a flat PDF. WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT FROM A REPLICA IS WHERE THE GEOMETRY COMES FROM: every rectangle, caption, column header and page break is the IRS template's own, laid out by an XFA engine, rather than measured and re-drawn by us. What it produces is still a RENDERING of the form and not the form — but for a document that is mailed or faxed, a printed rendering is what is filed. It is the cheapest route that keeps the IRS's own layout, and it is put forward as a candidate rather than a recommendation.
resolved.route_static_replica_and_why_it_is_NOT_a: A FILED DOCUMENT THAT IS NOT THE IRS FORM IS A DIFFERENT OBJECT FROM A FILLED IRS FORM. That sentence is the whole of it. The engineering cost is knowable and unremarkable — 331 cells, three pages, a layout this tree can already read out of the template. The question that is not ours is whether a document the Service receives may be one we drew, carrying the IRS's form number and revision, produced by a party that is not the IRS. It is a question for Principal and JLW and it is recorded here so that nobody answers it by building.
resolved.route_do_not_fill_it: HOLD THE DATA AND PRODUCE IT FOR A PREPARER OR ANOTHER CHANNEL. WHAT IT LEAVES UNDONE, STATED: somebody types 331 fields by hand into Adobe Reader, which is the only widely deployed renderer that opens this form at all; the engine can neither verify what they typed nor read it back, so the round-trip proof that stands on all six mapped forms does not exist here; and the "I R S Allowed" column, which the tree can compute from the standards file it already holds, is computed by a person instead. It costs nothing to adopt and it is the status quo.
resolved.how_a_433H_REVISION_WOULD_BE_PINNED_UNDE: IT CANNOT BE PINNED THE WAY EVERY OTHER FORM IS, AND THAT IS DECLARED RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND. The standing rule is that a revision is never asserted from anything but DRAWN PAGE BYTES. 433-H's one drawn page is 332 characters of "The document you are trying to load requires Adobe Reader 8 or higher" and carries no revision, no catalogue number and no form number. Every available source is packet-derived or metadata-derived: the template's product_id draw says "Form 433-H" and "(March 2025)"; its assist/speak says "Revised March 2025. Catalog Number 71232U"; the PDF /Info Title says "Form 433-H (Rev. 3-2025)"; the config packet's build path names f433-h--2025-03-00--web.pdf. FOUR SOURCES AGREEING IS NOT THE SAME KIND OF EVIDENCE AS ONE DRAWN LINE, because all four were written by the same authoring tool in the same file and none of them is what a filer reads off the page. Under routes A, A-prime and render: pin the DOCUMENT, not the revision — the blank's SHA-256 is 1da60f64ce39800219859be71dda7c7b29d1695e12998a3f061d65402fa154f8, it is recomputed on every run by [SB-26], and it answers the question the revision pin actually exists to answer, which is whether this is the same blank the work was done against. The revision string is recorded as PACKET-DERIVED and is never upgraded by being written down. Under a static replica: it cannot be pinned at all, because there is no IRS document in the artefact to pin.
resolved.which_question_we_are_actually_in: NOT "CAN WE FILL IT" — that is answered. The collection-information half of 433-H is 433-F, and 433-F is mapped, provisioned and round-tripping; the instalment-agreement half is 433-D, and 433-D is mapped and gated. The facts this form asks for are, with the one exception of a column we can compute ourselves, facts the backbone already holds or has a proved route to. SO THE QUESTION IS "DO WE NEED TO RENDER IT", AND THAT IS A QUESTION ABOUT CHANNEL AND ABOUT WHAT A FILED DOCUMENT MAY BE, NOT ABOUT THE ENGINE.
